## Implement these three dataflow/storage changes together

The selected basis is `recovery-cost-repair-foundation.md` in the PC campaign;
this self-contained instruction carries its implementation requirements so
you need not search unavailable/newer documents in this base checkout.

1. **Lazy features with ordered active indexes.** After `valid(s)` succeeds,
   build one bounded list of original camp indices satisfying exactly
   `known && alive && awake`, in original `Scene.camps` order. Keep the Scene
   intact. Compute/cache each requested local cell rather than all 49 cells.
   In one enemy loop compute distance once, adding to present and response
   independently in original enemy order and updating nearest with its old
   `100000` initial value. Then add indexed camp contributions in original
   order to present only. Preserve float types, initial zeros, comparisons,
   addition order within each accumulator and the complete Rank tuple/ties.
   Do not filter zero/negative/nonfinite Strength, switch to double, reassociate
   sums or add epsilons. All requested cells lie within the original local
   7x7 square by the unchanged candidate construction.
2. **Bounded owning endpoint lists.** Replace only the temporary endpoint
   vectors with ordered capacity-24 lists. Supported calls have range 1 or 2,
   hence 8 or 24 possible offsets. Retain dy/dx traversal, midpoint direction
   order, original actor origin in `physical`, origin returns, duplicate
   candidates, step/dash-first order and every physical/connectivity test.
   No truncation or changed raw/risk/effect counter. Do not change the separate
   `faster_home` BFS vectors or policy.
3. **Per-plan effect indexes.** Once per valid `select_plan`, index all known
   living camps in original index order; separately index valid-group known
   living asleep positive-strength members, and mark valid groups containing
   any unknown member. Preserve the old no-effect early result, footprint
   visibility (only in-map cells), enemy overlap, and invalid directly-hit-group
   rejection. A malformed unrelated group must not reject globally. Known
   living direct hits include awake/asleep/passive/zero-strength camps; do not
   substitute the active-risk list. Complete touched groups include far/dead/
   hidden/unknown siblings with the original rules. Any touched unknown group
   rejects. Stun without damage rejects any touched group, as before. Preserve
   the lazy one-effect-per-landing cache and `effect_unknown` increments.
   A 256-bit original-index waking set per cached effect may replace dynamic
   vectors; `extra` must enumerate original indices ascending and accumulate
   its float result separately from baseline risk. No pre-summed group floats
   or large landing-by-terminal-by-member table. Retain portions whose exact
   indexed equivalence cannot be established and report the specific gap.
